about.title: Benicia Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Benicia's mix of waterfront shops along First Street, aging apartment complexes, and busy retail centers near I-780 means uneven pavement, wet floors, and poor lighting show up more often than people expect. When a property owner knows about a hazard and doesn't fix it or warn visitors, California law may hold them responsible for resulting injuries. Proving that knowledge, or that the owner reasonably should have known, is often the hardest part of these cases, which is why documenting conditions right away matters. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects Benicia residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney experienced in premises liability claims. The attorney you're matched with can evaluate the property owner's responsibility, help gather surveillance footage before it's deleted, and explain your options. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you, and there's no obligation to move forward after speaking with them.

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California premises liability generally requires proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify evidence of prior complaints, maintenance logs, or similar incidents that establish this.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Benicia businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to showing exactly how and why the fall happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you're found partly responsible for the fall — your recovery is simply adjusted to reflect the percentage of fault assigned to you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Benicia?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or Benicia park, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical date.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near the marina or downtown First Street?
items.answer: Commercial property owners in Benicia's downtown and waterfront areas have the same duty to address known hazards as any other property owner. An independent attorney can look into maintenance records, prior incident reports, and store surveillance to evaluate whether the owner failed to act on a hazard they knew about.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to get help?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. There's no cost or obligation just to have a conversation about what happened.
